questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving boolean applications and parity.
questions.stem: In this exercise, a majority vote uses 7 voters and outputs one when more than half agree. Exactly how many input valuations produce an output of one?
questions.explanation: With 7 voters, exactly half of all 2 to the power 7 assignments have a majority of ones, giving 2 to the power 6 which equals 64. The required result is 64.
questions.hint: By symmetry half of all assignments have a majority of ones.

questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: In the given setup, for 8 input bits, in total how many valuations make the parity (the XOR of all bits) equal to one?
questions.explanation: Exactly half of the 2 to the power 8 bit strings have odd parity, so the number with parity one is 128. The required result is 128.
questions.hint: Half of all bit strings have odd parity.

questions.stem: In this exercise, for 4 input bits, exactly how many valuations make the parity (the XOR of all bits) equal to one?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "counts all assignments regardless of parity" gives 16, not 8.
Wrong belief "adds one extra assignment" gives 9, not 8.
Wrong belief "counts bits instead of assignments" gives 4, not 8.

questions.explanation: Exactly half of the 2 to the power 4 bit strings have odd parity, so the number with parity one is 8.
questions.hint: Half of all bit strings have odd parity.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving algorithm analysis and loop counting.
questions.stem: A nested loop runs i from 1 to 11 and j from 1 to i. How many times does the innermost body execute?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "assumes j always runs to n" gives 121, not 66.
Wrong belief "stops j one short of i" gives 55, not 66.
Wrong belief "counts only the outer iterations" gives 11, not 66.

questions.explanation: For each i the inner loop runs i times, so the total is 1 plus 2 plus up to 11, a triangular number equal to 66.
questions.hint: Sum 1 through n to count the inner iterations.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving algorithm analysis and loop counting.

stimulus.body: Binary search on a sorted list of 274 items uses at most how many comparisons in the worst case?

questions.stem: Binary search on a sorted list of 274 items uses at most how many comparisons in the worst case?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "rounds down and misses the last comparison" gives 8, not 9.
Wrong belief "allows one comparison too many" gives 10, not 9.
Wrong belief "doubles the halving count" gives 18, not 9.

questions.explanation: Each comparison roughly halves the search interval, so the worst-case number of comparisons is the ceiling of log base 2 of (274 plus 1), which is 9.
questions.hint: Count how many times n can be halved before reaching one.
